subject.title: [Feature]: Pattern-based channel allowlist for Discord (glob/wildcard support)

question: Should Discord guild allowlists support channel-name patterns, and if so what exact syntax and precedence should apply relative to exact entries, thread-parent fallback, and the literal `*` catch-all?
rationale: This changes the authorization boundary for inbound Discord messages, so an implementation cannot safely choose whether patterns are accepted, how overlaps resolve, or whether matching applies to IDs, names, and normalized slugs without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a narrow glob contract
options.body: Support a restricted documented glob syntax for channel names/slugs, with exact and parent entries taking precedence and a deterministic most-specific pattern rule.

options.title: Prefer category configuration
options.body: Decline name patterns and direct dynamic-channel workflows toward the separate category-level configuration proposal at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/60582.

options.title: Keep explicit entries only
options.body: Retain the current exact-entry and literal-wildcard authorization model to avoid adding another access-control grammar.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow glob contract
recommendation.body: Support a restricted documented glob syntax for channel names/slugs, with exact and parent entries taking precedence and a deterministic most-specific pattern rule.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared matcher and its precedence rules are the central decision surface, and prior history shows sustained work on that implementation.
